claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 20 years old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he is in approved education or training. Generally, you can only receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they are under 20 **and** staying in approved education or training.

However, since Alex is already 20, he has now passed the age limit for Child Benefit eligibility, even if he is in education or training.

Could you confirm whether Alex turned 20 recently, and if so, was he in approved education or training before his 20th birthday? This will help me give you a complete picture of your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 20 a few months ago. He's not in any education or training - he finished his A-levels a couple of years back and has been working part-time since then, just doing some shifts at the local shop on weekends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Based on what you've told me about Alex:

- He is 20 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He has been working part-time since finishing his A-levels

Unfortunately, this means you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

1. **Age requirement**: Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For those aged 16-19, eligibility continues only if they remain in approved education or training.

2. **Education/training status**: Since Alex finished his A-levels a couple of years ago and hasn't been in approved education or training since then, he wouldn't have qualified during that period either.

3. **Age limit**: Even if Alex were to return to education now, he has turned 20, which is the absolute cut-off age for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me now provide you with my formal eligibility assessment.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

Thank you for providing all the information I needed. I've now completed my assessment.

### Result for Alex: **Not Eligible** ❌

**Reasoning:**
- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16.
- For children aged 16-19, eligibility can only continue if they remain in approved education or training.
- Alex is 20 years old and has not been in approved education or training since finishing his A-levels a couple of years ago.
- At 20, Alex has exceeded the maximum age limit for Child Benefit, which is under 20 (and only applies if they stay in approved education or training).

**Summary:** Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex as he is now over the age limit and is not in approved education or training.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you have or become responsible for other children), please don't hesitate to ask.
